The Hiring  
Report | 2022
An overview of the UK’s startup and 
scaleup recruitment landscape

2
What does startup recruitment look like 
in 2022? According to Beauhurst’s own 
Recruitment Manager, Joe Hodgson:
The current state of 
startup and scaleup 
recruitment in the UK
“It’s a really interesting time for recruiters. The 
hiring market is very volatile at the minute, 
especially here in the UK—some companies 
have overextended themselves and are making 
redundancies, whilst others are thriving, raising 
large sums of investment and putting that towards 
recruitment drives. 
It’s a candidate-driven market right now, and the 
tech industry in particular is willing to pay over 
the odds to meet that shortfall. So it’s crucial for 
recruiters to find and latch on to those cash-rich 
companies with really strong growth trajectories 
(and not waste time on those that are struggling).” 
Around 30% of high-growth UK companies are 
expanding their teams right now—that’s nearly 
14k businesses on the lookout for new talent. This 
report explores the data on these companies, to 
spot key trends in the market.

03
What do we mean 
by high-growth?
We use eight different criteria to identify  
high-growth and ambitious businesses. Each of 
these is a sign that a company is actively growing 
or creating ambitious growth plans.  
 
All of the companies featured in this report have 
met at least one of our high-growth triggers, and 
are hence tracked on the Beauhurst platform.

04
How do we know 
that a business 
is hiring?
Beauhurst’s actively hiring data runs over all of our 45k+ 
tracked companies, and can be used within our Advanced 
Search feature to find the businesses most relevant to you. 
Our analysts use publicly available information to ascertain 
whether a company is currently hiring:
• The company itself must have open job roles (recruitment 
agencies hiring into client companies but not into 
themselves would not count) 
• A job listing must have a job title and/or job description 
• Job pages that only contain a generic message such as 
“we’re always looking for new talent—get in touch” are not 
sufficient
This data is essential for recruiters searching for new clients, 
but also accelerators and funds looking to track the success 
of their portfolios, and government bodies or LEPs wanting to 
understand the health of local business ecosystems.

05
Which UK regions have the most 
actively hiring companies?
London has both the greatest number of actively hiring 
companies (4,618) and the largest proportion, at 33% of 
its high-growth business population—tied with the East 
Midlands, despite its relatively small number of actively 
hiring companies (675). 
Wales and Scotland, on the other hand, have the lowest 
hiring rates. Even still, an impressive 1 in 4 companies are 
actively hiring in those regions (401 and 781 businesses, 
respectively). 
Hiring rates in the North East and South East also come 
in slightly below the national average, at 27%, while the 
remaining regions are in line with the wider UK (~30%).
At a local authority level, besides areas within London, 
Edinburgh and Leeds have the highest number of actively 
hiring companies in the UK.

Olsam
Olsam acquires FBA (Fulfilled by Amazon) 
e-commerce businesses, migrating assets such 
as website domains and software tools to its 
ownership. It then helps to scale these brands, 
providing capital investment and supply chain 
expertise.
Olsam has raised £121m in equity fundraisings 
so far, with its latest round in September 2021 
intended to invest in the company’s platform, 
expand its IP and patent protection, fund more 
acquisitions, and grow its operations team. In May 
2022, Olsam also acquired US e-commerce brand 
platform MarketFleet.
The company offers 30 days of holiday to new 
employees, regular team socials, and a flexible 
office space with drinks on tap, an on-site barista, 
and table tennis.

07
The most common stage 
of evolution for expanding 
companies 
Despite being the most negatively affected by 
COVID-19 at the beginning of the pandemic, 
Established-stage companies are now the most 
likely to be growing their teams. These tend to 
be older businesses (usually 15+ years), with 
multiple offices and a sustained turnover well 
into the millions. Nearly half (49%) of high-
growth companies that are actively hiring right 
now are operating at this stage.
Seed startups are the least likely to be 
recruiting right now, accounting for just 14% 
of actively hiring companies, while businesses 
operating at the Venture and Growth stages 
account for 19% and 18%, respectively.

Dubit
Dubit produces online games for use in the 
metaverse, specialising in esports and children’s 
gaming. The company develops research tools that 
assist its Consulting, Development and Marketing 
teams in incorporating a child’s perspective into 
the product development process. 
The Leeds-based games developer has been 
awarded £183k worth of Innovate UK grants so 
far. It has also secured one equity investment, in 
November 2021—the £5.90m fundraising saw 
participation from Brazilian fund Meta Ventures, 
alongside angel investors. With this funding, Dubit 
intends to launch a live esports league in the 
metaverse, initially on the Roblox platform. 
Dubit offers its employees 25 days holiday, 
company away days, and paid training and 
personal development.
08

09
Top sectors  
for startup and 
scaleup jobs 
Of the high-growth UK companies that are hiring right now, 
50% operate in Business & Professional Services. Particularly 
strong are the banking, marketing and recruitment sectors.
Meanwhile, 31% are Technology/IP-based businesses, which 
covers everything from software and cleantech to hardware 
and life sciences. Within this industry, we currently track 
1,419 software-as-a-service (SaaS) companies that are 
looking to grow their teams. 
Industrials is also a top industry, accounting for 24% of 
actively hiring companies in the UK. 
In contrast, just 10% operate in each of the Retail, Personal 
Services and Leisure & Entertainment spaces—perhaps 
unsurprising, given the challenges faced by these industries 
during COVID-19. Nonetheless, they still boast a large number 
of ambitious businesses that are looking to make new hires.

RegTick develops an online platform that

businesses. The compliance management 
platform was created for distributed teams 
in the financial services, healthcare and

collaborate on challenging projects from 
anywhere in the world.
In March 2022, the Belfast-based SaaS 
startup secured a £1.00m equity investment 
from Northern Irish businessman Tom 
O’Gorman. The investment will support 
RegTick to develop new products, scale 
internationally, and expand its tech team, 
creating 30 new jobs.
RegTick offers flexible working, with remote 
or hybrid options for all of its open roles.

How much more likely are  
VC-backed companies to be hiring? 
The UK is home to 5,737 actively hiring 
companies that have secured equity 
funding. This still leaves 8,071  
high-growth companies that are 
expanding their teams despite never 
raising equity finance. Roughly the same 
proportion of businesses that have raised 
equity investment are actively hiring than 
those without it (30-31%).
Having said that, when breaking the 
data down by investor type, companies 
backed by private equity or venture 
capital funds are considerably more 
likely to be recruiting than their peers: an 
impressive 53% of VC-backed businesses 
are actively hiring, compared to just 28% 
of companies that haven’t secured VC 
investment.

Pockit
Pockit produces prepaid credit cards that also 
provide discounts and cashback from associated 
retailers. The Welsh fintech company aims to 
make money simple for low-income, ‘unbanked’ 
customers. It attended both the Govstart and 
Upscale accelerator programmes in 2017 and has 
featured in several high-growth lists. 
To date, Pockit has raised £28.9m in equity 
investment, across 10 funding rounds. Investors 
include the North East Fund, Crowdcube, 
and VCT and private equity firm Maven. The 
company’s most recent fundraising was a £2.45m 
unannounced round, completed in February 2022. 
The company offers its employees 25 days of 
annual leave, Perkbox rewards, and regular 
company away days.

How to find

With Beauhurst, you could find thousands more 
actively hiring companies, in the time it took you 
to read this sentence.  
Using our Advanced Search feature, you can even 
filter down by criteria like location, sector, stage

You’ll then have access to extensive profiles for 
these businesses, plus verified contact details for 
key decision makers. That way, you can reach out 
to the right leads, at the right time, and be fully 
prepared for each conversation.
